2. These first bail applications have been moved by the applicants seeking regular bail in Case Crime/F.I.R. No.25 of 2024, under Section 420, 467, 468, 471 & 120-B I.P.C. and Section 66-D of the Information Technology Act, registered at Police Station Cyber PS, District Dehradun.

entities.text: Police Station Cyber PS, District Dehradun
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 3. It is contended by learned counsel for the applicants that applicants have falsely been implicated in the instant crime; have no criminal history and are languishing in jail since 09.05.2024.

Learned counsel for the applicants submits that there is no direct evidence in the F.I.R. that proves applicants' involvement in the alleged offence; that applicants neither conversed with the complainant nor have contacted him through any medium; that applicants neither demanded any money from the complainant nor have credited any money in their personal account; that the alleged recovery from the possession of the applicants is planted one.
They submit that in case, the applicants are granted bail, they will not misuse the same and will furnish the bail surety as 2025:UHC:3774 per the satisfaction of this Court.
4. Learned State Counsel vehemently opposed the bail application.

5. Considering the submission of learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion as to the final merits of the case, this Court is of the view that applicants deserve bail at this stage.

7. Let the applicant, namely, Ravi Saini, Rahul Kumar Dutta and Kapil Arora be released on bail, on executing personal bond by each one of them and furnishing two reliable sureties by each one of them, each of like amount, to the satisfaction of Court concerned.
